title: Terraform: refactor private GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking and state layout
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our Private Terraform modules for GPU node pools, IAM bindings, and networking have diverged across customers and create inconsistent state layouts. This causes painful state migrations and makes upgrades fragile for on-prem/VPC installs. This PR refactors the module layout to a opinionated, stable state layout and introduces a dedicated node_pools module with clearer IAM boundaries and explicit networking attachments.

Summary of changes: 
- Introduce modules/node_pools (encapsulates GPU pool lifecycle, autoscaling, taints/labels and node config).
- Move provider-agnostic state objects into state/layout.tf for deterministic remote state keys.
- Split iam/ into iam/roles.tf and iam/bindings.tf with least-privilege defaults for node role, kube-controller and CSI drivers.
- Networking: add networking/attachments.tf to explicitly wire subnets and route tables used by private deployments.
- Add migration helper scripts in examples/migrations/ to assist existing customers with state moves.
- Update README and examples to document new variables and the migration plan.

Why this approach: Making node pools a first-class module simplifies upgrade paths (we can replace individual pools without touching control-plane state), and a stable state layout reduces accidental key renames that forced manual state edits. Explicit IAM boundaries reduce blast radius for node-level credentials.

Checklist: 
- [x] Module split and re-exported top-level entrypoint (modules and examples updated)
- [x] Terraform validate + fmt passes
- [x] Integration run against a staging AWS account
- [x] Migration helper scripts included and documented
- [x] Runtime smoke tests for provisioning and rolling node replacement

Compatibility and migration notes: This change introduces a state layout migration for existing private installs. Migration is opt-in via the examples/migrations/migrate_state.sh script which runs a sequence of `terraform state mv` operations and verifies resource counts. We do not automatically rewrite state. New installs will use the new layout by default.

Rollout plan: 
1. Merge to main and cut a patch release for redwood-terraform.
2. Notify customers with Private installs and provide migration script + support window.
3. Encourage trial on staging clusters before production migration.

Rollback: If post-migration issues are observed, customers can restore the remote state from the pre-migration S3/GCS backup (migration guide explicitly instructs to backup remote state). The modules also allow re-mapping back to the legacy layout by setting the `legacy_state_mode` var (documented) but that path is discouraged.

Security considerations: IAM changes reduce cluster-scoped node permissions; we audited roles and tightened policies for CSI and NVIDIA drivers. The migration script does not change IAM bindings automatically; it only moves state keys.

Testing performed: 
- Manual staging deploys (us-west-2) provisioning 2 GPU node pools with mixed GPU types.
- Integration tests: terraform-aws-integration pipeline (ran end-to-end), one flaky networking test required a fix to attachments.tf and was re-run.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on state/layout.tf, modules/node_pools, and iam/bindings.tf for correctness. The largest risk is state migration semantics and potential for drifting resource addresses; migration script includes verification steps.

chore(state): consolidate remote state keys under state/layout.tf
feat(iam): split roles and bindings, tighten node role policy
fix(networking): ensure subnet attachment respects az distribution
docs(migrations): add migration scripts and upgrade guide
test(integration): add e2e smoke tests for node pool replacement

Author response: updated variables.tf and README with explicit guidance and defaults
Miguel Hernandez: asked for state migration dry-run mode — added verification step to migrate_state.sh
Omar Khaled: approved after IAM policy tightening and adding unit test for role document
release_notes: Refactor private Terraform layout: new node_pools module, stable state layout, IAM split. BREAKING: state migration required for existing private installs; migration helper included.
upgrade_instructions: 1) Backup remote state (S3/GCS) using `terraform state pull > backup.tfstate`. 2) Run examples/migrations/migrate_state.sh --dry-run and review mappings. 3) Run script without --dry-run to perform `terraform state mv` operations. 4) Apply modules on a staging workspace and validate node counts and IAM bindings. 5) Schedule production migration during maintenance window.
security_implications: Tightens node IAM policies and reduces cluster-scoped permissions. Migration does not modify IAM bindings automatically; operators must apply IAM plan after state migration. Recommended to review generated IAM plan before apply.
testing: Staging manual runs and CI integration pipeline. smoke tests validate rolling replacement, GPU driver init, and CSI mount. Logs and metrics collected in staging for 48h after provisioning.
notes: This PR intentionally does not change provider plugins or versions; recommend bumping terraform provider versions in a follow-up once state layout is stable.
